plain.text: Lazarus, who lived in Bethany with his sisters Mary and Martha, was sick. The sisters sent word: "Lord, the one you love is sick." Jesus said this sickness would not end in death, but was for God's glory. Jesus loved Martha, her sister and Lazarus. Yet he stayed where he was two more days. Then he told his disciples, "Lazarus has fallen asleep, but I am going to wake him up." He told them plainly, "Lazarus is dead." Thomas said, "Let us also go, that we may die with him."

When Jesus arrived, Lazarus had been in the tomb four days. Martha went out to meet him: "Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died." Jesus said, "Your brother will rise again." She said she knew he would rise at the last day. Jesus said, "I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in me will live, even though they die. Do you believe this?" "Yes, Lord," she said, "I believe that you are the Christ, the Son of God."

Mary came, fell at Jesus' feet and said the same words: "Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died." When Jesus saw her weeping, he was deeply moved and troubled. "Where have you laid him?" he asked. Jesus wept. People said, "See how he loved him!" Others asked why he hadn't kept him from dying.

At the tomb, a cave with a stone across the entrance, Jesus said, "Take away the stone." Martha said there would be a bad smell. Jesus said, "Did I not tell you that if you believe, you will see the glory of God?" Jesus prayed aloud, then called in a loud voice, "Lazarus, come out!" The dead man came out, wrapped in strips of linen. Jesus said, "Unwrap him and let him go."

Many who saw this believed. But some told the Pharisees. The council met, worried that everyone would believe in him and the Romans would destroy the temple and nation. The high priest Caiaphas said it was better for one man to die for the people than for the whole nation to perish. John explains that, without realising, he was prophesying that Jesus would die for the nation, and for God's scattered children. From that day they plotted to kill him. As Passover approached, people wondered if Jesus would come to the feast.

summary.bigIdea: Jesus is the resurrection and the life; he weeps with the grieving and raises Lazarus from the dead.
points: "I am the resurrection and the life."
Jesus wept with Mary and Martha.
Lazarus comes out of the tomb, and the leaders decide Jesus must die.
summary.reflection: Jesus wept even though he knew he would raise Lazarus. What does that tell you about how God sees your grief?
